mainEntity.name: What is fractional PR for a cybersecurity company?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fractional PR for a cybersecurity company is a senior PR operator working directly with the founder, CMO, or CISO on a part-time retainer, in place of a full agency. The operator handles narrative positioning, analyst relations with Gartner, Forrester, IDC and KuppingerCole, tier-1 security press outreach (Dark Reading, SC Media, CyberScoop, The Record, SecurityWeek), threat-research amplification, coordinated vulnerability disclosure communications, and founder profiling. For security startups pre-Series B this typically replaces a $20,000 to $35,000 per month agency retainer with $5,000 to $12,000 per month for the same scope, because there is no account-team layer to fund.

mainEntity.name: How is cybersecurity PR different from generic tech PR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Three differences. First, analyst relations is load-bearing, not optional: Gartner, Forrester, IDC and KuppingerCole shape buyer shortlists, so a security PR program that cannot name the analysts covering SASE, XDR, identity or cloud security is not a real program. Second, the news engine is threat research, not product launches: a vendor's own threat report, CVE disclosure, or incident-response data is what security journalists at Dark Reading, CyberScoop and The Record actually publish. Third, breach and disclosure comms must be in scope from day one — security companies operate in a category where a coordinated disclosure or a customer incident can land on any given week, and the communications response is part of the brand, not a separate emergency.

mainEntity.name: How much does cybersecurity PR cost in 2026?

acceptedAnswer.text: Fractional senior PR for a cybersecurity company in 2026 runs $5,000 to $12,000 per month. The median monthly retainer paid by Series B cybersecurity companies to a senior-led traditional PR agency in 2025-2026 is around $23,500, because that retainer funds a multi-person account team and a separate analyst-relations specialist. Analyst-relations sprints (8 to 12 weeks of structured Gartner, Forrester and IDC briefings around a launch or a Magic Quadrant or Wave cycle) range $12,000 to $28,000. Disclosure or launch sprints (4 to 8 weeks around a funding round, a major CVE, or a threat-report release) range $15,000 to $40,000. The model that fits most security startups pre-Series B is a 3 to 6 month fractional retainer with an analyst-relations sprint stacked on the briefing window.

mainEntity.name: Can a fractional operator run analyst relations with Gartner and Forrester?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — analyst relations is structured work, not a relationship monopoly. The deliverable is a briefing calendar mapped to the Magic Quadrant and Forrester Wave cycles for the vendor's category, a vendor briefing deck written to the questions analysts actually ask, inquiry sessions booked against the research agenda, and a feedback loop that feeds analyst objections back into product and messaging. A fractional operator runs that process directly with the founder in the room, instead of routing it through an account team. What a fractional model does not promise is a guaranteed Magic Quadrant position — no honest operator promises that, because analysts score the product, not the pitch.

mainEntity.name: Why does AI search visibility matter for cybersecurity vendors?

acceptedAnswer.text: Security buyers — CISOs, security engineers, GRC leads — now run vendor research through ChatGPT, Perplexity, Claude and Google AI Overviews before they ever reach a sales call. When a buyer asks an AI engine 'best XDR vendors' or 'who does CTEM well', the answer is assembled from earned editorial coverage, analyst mentions, and structured content, not from the vendor's own marketing pages. Independent research in 2026 consistently finds that earned editorial coverage accounts for the large majority of links AI engines cite, while press releases account for roughly one percent. A cybersecurity PR program built for 2026 produces the earned coverage and the named-author, schema-structured content that AI engines retrieve — so the vendor appears in the answer, not just in the ten blue links nobody clicks.

mainEntity.name: Do you handle breach communications and incident response PR?

acceptedAnswer.text: Yes — and for a cybersecurity vendor it has to be in scope before it is needed. Breach and incident communications cover three scenarios: a security incident at the vendor itself, a coordinated vulnerability disclosure the vendor is releasing, and a customer incident where the vendor's product is named in coverage. The work is a pre-built holding-statement library, a disclosure-timeline template aligned to coordinated-disclosure norms, a named-spokesperson and approval chain, and a journalist contact map so the response goes out in hours, not days. The goal is that the communications response is rehearsed, not improvised, because in security the improvised response is the story.

mainEntity.name: How does cybersecurity PR work in Korea in 2026 (KISA, PIPC, named outlets, K-Shield)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Korean cybersecurity press runs through Boannews, Daily Secu, Security News Korea, ChosunBiz security desk and ZDNet Korea security; analyst-relations work routes through KISA (Korea Internet & Security Agency) and Gartner Korea, not the US desks. The buyer frame is the Personal Information Protection Commission disclosure rules, the K-Shield enterprise certification, the K-ISMS information-security management system, and the Korea Communications Commission incident-reporting timeline (24-hour breach notification). Korean CISOs ask AI engines in Korean before vendor calls, and Naver SGE prefers Korean-original Boannews and Daily Secu citations over translated Western coverage, so the program needs at least one Korean-original threat-research brief or named-CVE disclosure before the AI Overviews entity graph picks up the vendor for category queries.

mainEntity.name: How does cybersecurity PR work in Japan in 2026 (METI, JPCERT/CC, ITmedia Security, Hardening Project)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Japanese cybersecurity press anchors on ITmedia Security, Nikkei Cross Tech Security desk, ScanNetSecurity, Security NEXT and the IT Media Enterprise security beat. The buyer frame is the METI Cybersecurity Management Guidelines v3.0, the JPCERT/CC coordinated-disclosure standard, the NISC Cybersecurity Strategy, and the Cabinet Office Active Cyber Defense bill the Diet passed in 2025. Japanese CISOs weigh vendors against named enterprise pilots (Mitsubishi UFJ, NTT Communications, KDDI, Rakuten Group) before they take the brief. The Hardening Project (community-led security competition) and CODE BLUE Tokyo (October) are the named-researcher convergence cycles; a JPCERT-coordinated CVE disclosure is the highest-leverage news event a foreign vendor can land in Japan, beating any product-launch press release on AI-citation share.

mainEntity.name: How does cybersecurity PR work in Singapore in 2026 (CSA, MAS TRM, Black Hat Asia, RSAC APJ)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Singapore cybersecurity press runs through CNA Insider security, The Business Times tech-security desk, Computer Weekly Asia, and the regional desks of Dark Reading Asia and SC Media APAC. The buyer frame is the Cyber Security Agency (CSA) Cybersecurity Code of Practice for CII, the MAS Technology Risk Management Guidelines (2021 with the 2025 cloud-resilience update), the Cybersecurity Act, and the SG Cyber Safe trust mark. Black Hat Asia (April, Marina Bay Sands) and RSA Conference APJ (July, Singapore) are the named-researcher convergence cycles; the CSA Singapore International Cyber Week (October) is the policy-and-buyer convergence cycle. MAS TRM alignment is the credibility frame for FinTech security vendors — without an MAS-licensed pilot or a CSA-recognized cybersecurity-services provider tie, top-tier Singapore editors treat the brief as a US press release in English.

mainEntity.name: How does cybersecurity PR work in Dubai and MENA in 2026 (Dubai Electronic Security Center, GISEC, NCA Saudi)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Dubai and MENA cybersecurity press runs through Tahawultech, IntelligentCIO Middle East, CPI Media Group's Security Middle East, Gulf News tech desk and Arabian Business Tech; Arabic-language depth comes from Asharq Business security and Al Arabiya tech. The buyer frame is the UAE Information Assurance Standards (NESA), the Dubai Electronic Security Center (DESC) framework, the Saudi National Cybersecurity Authority (NCA) Essential Cybersecurity Controls (ECC-2:2024), and the Saudi Data and AI Authority (SDAIA) data-protection layer. GISEC Global (May, Dubai World Trade Centre) is the regional buyer-and-press convergence cycle; the Saudi @Hack (October, Riyadh) is the NCA-aligned cycle. Saudi vendor access routes through Riyadh-based agencies because direct outreach without a local fiduciary fails the Communications, Space and Technology Commission filter.

mainEntity.name: How does cybersecurity PR work in India in 2026 (CERT-In, DPDP Act, Nullcon, c0c0n)?

acceptedAnswer.text: Indian cybersecurity press runs through ET CISO, Inc42 security desk, MoneyControl Tech security, The Hindu BusinessLine Cyber, CIO India and Express Computer; technical depth comes from Nullcon and c0c0n researcher coverage. The buyer frame is the Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In) Cybersecurity Directions (April 2022 with 2025 amendments — 6-hour breach notification), the Digital Personal Data Protection Act 2023, the National Cyber Security Policy, the Reserve Bank of India cyber-resilience framework for regulated entities, and the SEBI cybersecurity and cyber-resilience framework for the capital markets. Nullcon Goa (March) and c0c0n Kochi (October) are the named-researcher convergence cycles. Indian enterprise buyers expect CERT-In empanelment or a named BFSI pilot (HDFC, ICICI, SBI, Axis) before the technical desk takes a Series B-stage foreign vendor brief.
